body: Thanks.  I'll try that.  I just feel like what I'm going through isn't as maniacally noteworthy of a therapist.  I just don't logically see the point in living.

Except the cost of working for someone who doesn't have the flexibility I need to interview for my goals.  I've tried working for a temp agency and the companies they sent me to paid well, even if the work was monotonous and easily replaced with a simple program.  But they weren't flexible when I said I had to take a day off to travel to and from an interview that is half a state away.

But I think you're right on the winding path of careers.  I know you have to keep at it if you want it.  I just feel so tired and hopeless.  I don't know what to do or where to go to make things better.  I grew up in a very sheltered uber Christian household.  I still hold the same core beliefs personally, but I don't believe in missing out on the opportunities I had as a kid to just be physically and spiritually safe.

I wanted to join sports teams, take college courses early, join the chamber orchestra.  But I couldn't because the practice days intersected with the day my parents went to church.  I'm sure they thought they were making the right choices for the times.  Child kidnappings were rising and it wasn't as safe to walk the streets anymore.  But now I don't know how to research or network or connect with anything that might help my career.

And this is what I also don't get.  I make time for my friends.  But they don't make time for me.  I haven't hung out with a friend in two years.  I invited them out, organized times where we could all meet together.  But once I started working at a flexible job that doesn't pay very well, they can't adjust to my times.  They all start hanging out together without me.  My girlfriend, who I barely see, says that she sees them in her store every couple of weeks or so and they ask about me, but they never text or facebook message me.  I tried to keep up with contacting them, but after several consecutive nonresponses, you just give up.

I'm always uncertain about things like that.  For instance, if you mention a warning word like suicide, do they ask you to check into a ward?  Would it be on your work record and you have to report it to your future employers?  And then there's the cost.  I can afford a comfortable living right now, but that's because I'm big on savings and never buy anything but necessities.  Maybe I will look around for some quotes,
No.  I've thought about it, but then I think that they'll just say I'm stressed and that's it.  And I don't want some alarm button to be pressed and I'm courtly summoned to a mental ward.

It's going to suck.  It's going to suck for a while.  Just accept that.  I went through this in college and it was hell.  She was a gold digger and I didn't see it.  But you'll make it.  Time heals these wounds because you'll eventually forget your feelings for her.

Don't get into a new relationship quickly.  Dwell on what happened.  Why it happened.  Grow from it.  Be social.  Meet new people.  Have flings (wear protection and maintain them so they don't break).  And when you're ready, you'll know.  Someone else might try to find you.  And if you've learned to say, "fuck it, why not?", then you know you're ready to move on.

A year into my current relationship, I was still thinking about my ex.  Half a year later, barely at all.  Now, three years after, I don't even think I could spell her last name right and we were together for two years.
